description: Text that steers a model against its developer's intent. **Direct** when the user types it, **indirect** when it hides in content the model reads (web pages, email, documents, tool results).
Simon Willison's name for an agent that combines access to private data, exposure to untrusted content and a way to communicate externally. Together they let one injection steal data; remove a leg.
Data leaving the system through a channel the attacker controls: a markdown image URL, a link, a tool call with data in its arguments.
Every tool and credential gets only the access its task needs, for as short a time as possible.
Instructions hidden in a tool's description or schema, read by the model but rarely by the user.
A check on what enters or leaves the model: classifiers, PII redaction, length and topic limits. Probabilistic, so one layer among several.
Attacking your own system on purpose, ideally as an automated adversarial eval suite that gates releases.
Assets, trust boundaries, entry points, threats mapped to mitigations, and the residual risk you accept.
